short.q: What is an asana?
short.answer: A body posture.

short.q: Give the date and origin of International Yoga Day.
short.answer: 21 June, chosen by the United Nations.
short.working: 1 mark for the date, 1 mark for the United Nations.

short.q: Give two safety rules for yoga.
short.answer: Practise with a teacher, wear loose clothes, do it on a mat, do not do it after a big meal, stop if you feel dizzy (any two).

short.q: Why should children do Bhastrika and Kapaal Bhaati gently?
short.answer: They are active breathing exercises, so children need a teacher and must stop when tired.

short.q: Describe how to do Bhastrika.
short.answer: Sit tall, breathe in deeply through the nose, breathe out through the nose with the same force, repeat slowly a few times, and rest.
short.working: 1 mark for sitting tall, 1 mark for equal in and out breaths, 1 mark for slow and rest.

short.q: Explain the meaning of Kapaal Bhaati.
short.answer: Kapaal means forehead and bhaati means shining, so it means shining forehead. The breath goes out in short pushes and breathing in happens by itself.
short.working: 1 mark each for meaning, quick breath out and automatic breath in.

short.q: Describe how to sit in Vajra Asana.
short.answer: Kneel with knees together, bring big toes close, sit back on your heels, keep the back and head straight and place palms on the thighs.
short.working: 1 mark each for three correct steps.

short.q: Give three benefits of yoga.
short.answer: It keeps the body flexible and strong, helps us breathe well and stay calm, helps us focus and teaches discipline (any three).

short.q: Describe how to do Sasankasana.
short.answer: Start in Vajra Asana, breathe in and raise the arms, breathe out and bend forward, rest the forehead on the mat with arms stretched forward, breathe calmly and come up slowly.
short.working: 1 mark each for four correct steps.

short.q: Explain why yoga should be practised with an expert.
short.answer: An expert shows the correct posture, corrects mistakes, prevents strain of the back or knees, and knows when to stop.

short.q: Suggest four activities for celebrating International Yoga Day in school.
short.answer: Doing yoga together, taking photos or videos, making a chart of asanas, making a guidance video with an adult (any four).

short.q: Explain how learners can include friends with special needs in yoga.
short.answer: They can do breathing slowly, take seated poses, help hold the chart or take photos, and be encouraged by their partners. Everyone's effort is respected.
short.working: 1 mark for each of four points and 1 mark for respect.

short.q: Compare Vajra Asana and Sasankasana.
short.answer: Vajra Asana is sitting on the heels with a straight back. Sasankasana starts in Vajra Asana and bends forward with the forehead on the mat and arms stretched forward. Both are calm and use steady breathing.
short.working: 2 marks for each pose and 1 mark for a similarity.

short.q: List three things you should do before starting yoga.
short.answer: Wear loose clothes, prepare a mat, have an empty stomach, find a quiet place, meet with a teacher (any three).

short.q: Why should we breathe slowly during asanas?
short.answer: It keeps us calm and helps the body relax.

short.q: What is Dharma?
short.answer: The right way of living, including duty, honesty and kindness.

short.q: List the five principles of Dharma studied in the lesson.
short.answer: Paramatma, Purushartha, Prani Daya, Punarjanam, Prarthana (any correct set earns marks).
short.working: Half a mark for each, rounded up.

short.q: Name the four Purusharthas.
short.answer: Dharma, Artha, Kama, Moksha.

short.q: What does Prani Daya mean?
short.answer: Kindness to all living beings.
short.working: 1 mark each for kindness and living beings.

short.q: Explain the meaning of the word Paramatma.
short.answer: The Supreme Soul, or God.

short.q: Explain what Punarjanam means.
short.answer: Punarjanam is rebirth. The soul does not die but takes a new body until it reaches Moksha.
short.working: 1 mark for rebirth, 1 mark for the soul, 1 mark for Moksha.

short.q: Explain the meaning of karma.
short.answer: Karma means action. Good actions bring good results and unkind actions bring trouble.
short.working: 1 mark for action, 1 mark for good, 1 mark for unkind.

short.q: Write three ways in which a child can practise Prani Daya.
short.answer: Give water to thirsty animals, share food, help a hurt friend, do not harm insects, care for plants (any three).

short.q: Give three reasons why prayer is a principle of Dharma.
short.answer: It makes us thankful, calm and humble, gives courage, and reminds us we are not alone (any three).

short.q: Explain how the story of Prahlad shows faith in Paramatma.
short.answer: Prahlad believed God is everywhere, kept praying when his father was angry, and was protected.

short.q: Explain the four Purusharthas with one example each for a child.
short.answer: Dharma: doing homework and telling the truth. Artha: saving pocket money honestly. Kama: enjoying play and friendship. Moksha: praying and growing kind.

short.q: Describe the story of King Shibi and the dove and give its lesson.
short.answer: A frightened dove flew into the king's lap and a hawk demanded it. The king offered his own flesh to save the dove. The lesson is that a kind person protects the weak.
short.working: 1 mark for the dove, 1 mark for the hawk, 1 mark for the offer, 1 mark for the lesson.

short.q: Describe how to pray well.
short.answer: Sit quietly, fold hands, think of God with love, say thanks, ask for wisdom and kindness, and end with a promise to do good (any four).

short.q: Describe how a child can follow all five principles in one day.
short.answer: Morning prayer and Namaste (Prarthana, Paramatma), honest schoolwork (Dharma, Artha), helping a friend (Prani Daya), thinking about the day's good deeds (Punarjanam and karma).
short.working: 1 mark for each principle applied, up to 5.

short.q: Explain why balance is important in the four Purusharthas.
short.answer: Wealth and wishes are good but must follow Dharma. Without balance, chasing money or wishes can lead to cheating and harm, while Dharma keeps us honest.
short.working: 1 mark for balance, 2 marks for Dharma guiding the others, 2 marks for an example.

short.q: Why should we respect others who have different beliefs about death?
short.answer: People hold different views, listening with respect keeps peace, and arguing does not help.

short.q: What do the words Param and atma mean?
short.answer: Param means highest and atma means soul.

short.q: What is a festival?
short.answer: A special day or set of days when people come together to remember something important.
short.working: 1 mark for special day and 1 mark for remembering or celebrating together.

short.q: What is a rite or ritual? Give one example.
short.answer: A special action done in a set way at a festival, such as lighting a lamp or raising a flag.
short.working: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for example.

short.q: Give the meaning of Maha Shivratri.
short.answer: The great night of Lord Shiva.
short.working: 1 mark for great night and 1 mark for Shiva.

short.q: State two things people do on Maha Shivratri.
short.answer: Fast, stay awake all night, bathe the Shiva Linga, offer bel leaves, chant Om Namah Shivaya (any two).

short.q: Explain the words Micchami Dukkadam said at Paryushan.
short.answer: May any harm I did in thought, word or deed be forgiven.

short.q: On which date is Madaraka Day and what does Madaraka mean?
short.answer: 1 June; power or authority to govern.

short.q: Explain the importance of celebrating Madaraka Day.
short.answer: It reminds us of Kenya's step to self-government on 1 June 1963, teaches patriotism and unity, and lets us respect the flag and the anthem.

short.q: Describe how Paryushan Parva is celebrated.
short.answer: Jains fast, pray and meditate, listen to scriptures such as the Kalpasutra, practise Ahimsa, give to the needy and ask for forgiveness.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct practice, up to 3.

short.q: Describe how Maha Shivratri is celebrated.
short.answer: People fast, keep an all-night vigil, bathe the Shiva Linga with water and milk, offer bel leaves, chant Om Namah Shivaya and visit the Mandir.

short.q: State three ways of showing respect to the National flag and Anthem.
short.answer: Stand straight, be quiet, never let the flag touch the ground, learn and sing the anthem (any three).

short.q: Give three safety measures to observe during festivals.
short.answer: Adults light lamps, stay with adults in crowds, wash hands before eating, use bins, walk and do not run (any three).

short.q: Distinguish between Madaraka Day and Jamhuri Day.
short.answer: Madaraka Day is 1 June and marks internal self-government in 1963. Jamhuri Day is 12 December and marks independence in 1963 and the republic in 1964.
short.working: 1 mark for each date and 1 mark for a difference.

short.q: Explain what Maha Shivratri teaches.
short.answer: Self-control through fasting, faith through prayer, staying alert to do good, and thinking about our mistakes and trying to be better.

short.q: Explain why forgiveness is important, using Paryushan Parva.
short.answer: Forgiveness removes anger, mends friendships and brings peace. On the last day Jains ask everyone for forgiveness with Micchami Dukkadam.
short.working: 1 mark for each of four points.

short.q: Explain how a school can make festivals inclusive.
short.answer: Give clear instructions, help learners with special needs to take part, share food and clothes with the needy, and invite all faiths and communities.

short.q: Draw a timeline from January to December and mark Maha Shivratri, Madaraka Day and Paryushan.
short.answer: A line from January to December with Maha Shivratri in February or March, Madaraka Day on 1 June and Paryushan in August or September.
short.working: 1 mark for the line and months, 1 mark for each correct festival.

short.q: Compare the three festivals: Maha Shivratri, Paryushan Parva and Madaraka Day.
short.answer: Maha Shivratri is Hindu, a night of prayer for Shiva. Paryushan is Jain, of fasting and forgiveness. Madaraka Day is national, about self-government and patriotism. All bring people together.
short.working: 2 marks for correct faith or type, 2 marks for themes, 1 mark for a similarity.

short.q: Write a short composition on a festival of your choice.
short.answer: Any well-organised composition naming the festival, when it is held, what people do, what it teaches and how you feel.
short.working: 1 mark each for name, timing, activities, meaning, and feeling.

short.q: Why should we visit a friend's festival respectfully?
short.answer: We listen, ask polite questions, do not laugh at customs, and build peace among communities.

short.q: Which festival in the lesson is a national holiday and why?
short.answer: Madaraka Day, because it marks a step in Kenya's history and all Kenyans celebrate it.

short.q: Describe what the Panchang is.
short.answer: The Indian traditional calendar book that lists days, months and festival dates.

short.q: Write the Indian names for Sunday and Monday.
short.answer: Sunday: Ravivaar. Monday: Somvaar.

short.q: Write the Indian names for Tuesday and Wednesday.
short.answer: Tuesday: Mangalvaar. Wednesday: Budhvaar.

short.q: Write the Indian names for Thursday and Friday.
short.answer: Thursday: Guruvaar. Friday: Shukravaar.

short.q: Which day is Shanivaar and which planet is it linked with?
short.answer: Saturday, linked with Saturn.

short.q: Name two grahas in the traditional calendar that are not planets in modern science.
short.answer: The Sun and the Moon.

short.q: Match the days to the heavenly bodies: Ravivaar, Somvaar, Mangalvaar.
short.answer: Sun, Moon, Mars.

short.q: Match the days to the planets: Budhvaar, Guruvaar, Shukravaar.
short.answer: Mercury, Jupiter, Venus.

short.q: Explain how the days of the week are related to the solar system.
short.answer: They are named after the Sun, the Moon and five planets that people could see in the sky, so each day has a heavenly partner.
short.working: 1 mark each for Sun and Moon, planets and naming.

short.q: Give three uses of the Indian traditional calendar.
short.answer: Fixing festival dates, choosing days for prayers and family events, keeping tradition alive (any three).

short.q: Write the seven days of the week in the Indian traditional calendar with their heavenly bodies.
short.answer: Ravivaar: Sun; Somvaar: Moon; Mangalvaar: Mars; Budhvaar: Mercury; Guruvaar: Jupiter; Shukravaar: Venus; Shanivaar: Saturn.
short.working: Award 1 mark for every two correct pairs, up to 4.

short.q: Describe how to make a decorated calendar.
short.answer: Draw a table with seven columns, write English and Indian names, draw the Sun, Moon and planets above their days, and decorate it.

short.q: List four facts about the planets linked with the days.
short.answer: Mercury is closest to the Sun; Mars is the red planet; Jupiter is the largest; Saturn has rings (any four).

short.q: Explain why the Indian traditional calendar is special and how a child can use it.
short.answer: It links daily life to the sky and seasons, keeps tradition alive and fixes festival dates. A child can make a weekly plan, a decorated calendar, greeting cards or a song.
short.working: 2 marks for why it is special and 3 marks for uses.

short.q: Write a weekly plan using English and Indian day names with one activity for each of three days.
short.answer: Any correct plan, for example Somvaar: help at home; Guruvaar: thank a teacher; Shukravaar: share with a friend.
short.working: 1 mark for the format and 1 mark each for three correct day names with activities.

short.q: Name the months of the Indian traditional calendar in which Maha Shivratri and Paryushan fall.
short.answer: Maha Shivratri in Phalguna and Paryushan in Bhadrapada.
short.working: 1 mark each and 1 mark for correct spelling.

short.q: Why do the festival dates in this calendar change from year to year on our usual calendar?
short.answer: The months follow the Moon, so the dates move.
